product.audience: Collectors evaluating a limited hand-finished mechanical watch
product.decision: Understand the calibre architecture, finishing, configuration and allocation process
product.conversion: Configure a numbered watch and submit a private allocation request

signature.moment: A scroll-linked 3D mechanical movement opens from a complete watch into bridges, gears, jewels and hands, then returns to a collector configuration

systems.hero: An off-centre technical title ledger and live 3D watch on a bounded vertical calibre bench, not a photographic poster
systems.navigation: Slim numbered atelier rail with direct chapter coordinates and allocation status
systems.contentDensity: Dense technical notations around one spacious spatial object, followed by compact certificate and configuration surfaces
systems.geometry: Concentric case rings, radial callouts, exploded z-axis layers, ruled timing slips and jeweller tray divisions
systems.motion: Scroll opens the movement on its physical axis; explicit crown and layer controls update time and assembly state; no autoplay rotation
systems.coreInteraction: Visitors scrub the movement assembly, isolate functional layers, wind the crown, then configure case and strap for a visible allocation dossier

structuralDifferences: The first fold leads with a square loupe viewport and thumb crown before the atelier statement
The desktop scroll-linked exploded bench becomes explicit assembled, train and open buttons
Radial desktop annotations become a vertical numbered parts tray
The collector configuration resolves as an in-flow certificate rather than a side drawer

artDirection.typography: Condensed system grotesk for calibre numerals, quiet serif for watchmaker notes and monospaced timing data
artDirection.material: Graphite bench felt, rhodium bridges, warm brass train, synthetic ruby jewels and sapphire-blue focus marks
artDirection.imageLogic: All hero and movement imagery is code-native WebGL geometry; CSS provides loupe glass, timing slips and engraved rules
artDirection.microcopy: Bridge, barrel, train, escapement, beat error, amplitude, anglage, reserve and allocation language
artDirection.dataHonesty: Calibre, timing and production figures are clearly fictional sample atelier data

assetStrategy: A coordinated two-frame horology campaign supports the interactive calibre: one macro proof frame and one human-scale wrist frame, both original, local and compositionally distinct from the 3D assembly.

assets.role: Hand-finishing proof beside the finishing loupe
assets.focalCrop: Movement bridge and ruby bearing remain in the central-right field
assets.mobileSafeArea: Bearing, tool tip and metal grain remain readable in a portrait crop

assets.role: Quiet collector-scale campaign frame near configuration
assets.focalCrop: Watch and cuff occupy the left two-thirds with dark negative space
assets.mobileSafeArea: Dial, crown and cuff stay inside the middle 70 percent

adjacentTemplates.why: The existing watch is a photographic four-scene scroll film and allocation drawer; this is an operational 3D calibre bench with inline certificate.
No campaign portrait or jewellery gallery; the object is decomposed as a functional mechanical system.
Both use spatial geometry, but this radial horology bench, crown setting and chronometry certificate differ from gait calibration and chassis anatomy.
A z-axis calibre explosion and timing dossier replace room placement, swatch wallet and reservation flow.
No cinematic road story or trim atelier; the signature is a microscopic mechanism and collector certificate.

avoid: Copied Swiss brand language or marks
